title: A small cross-center ST–heart-rate interaction gain is sensitive to training uncertainty and ridge parameterization
abstract: An explicit ST-depression × age-normalized peak-heart-rate deficit term was tested beyond conventional clinical/exercise measures in historical public angiography data. Cleveland-trained models were applied without target fitting to independently collected Hungarian, Swiss and VA center databases. Hungarian AUC increased from0.87534 to0.87867 (difference0.00333; fixed-model paired bootstrap95% interval0.00076 to0.00611), but resampling both training and target samples gave an interval −0.01362 to0.01872. Orthogonalizing the added term while retaining the same augmented predictor span reversed its Hungarian gain (difference −0.00161). Swiss performance worsened. The findings establish a small fixed-fit, ridge-geometry-sensitive result, not a robust new physiological marker or clinical benefit. Participant identity is unavailable; duplicate and zero-cholesterol sensitivities, isolated clean reruns, public input hashes and autonomous AI authorship are documented.
